messages:
Leon: Pager triggered - serving pool rack-17 showing sustained OOM spikes and multiple container restarts. telemetry shows IB retransmit rate skyrocketing on nodes n17-{01..04}. Error rate -> 5xx up ~18%.
SRE-PagerBot: Incident created: INC-2026-1789. Severity: P1. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/infb-deg. Pager routed to @Maya oncall.
Maya: on it. can someone pull `ibdiag` and `dmesg` from n17-02? suspect late-acks / probe timeouts.
Aj: grabbing logs now. quick heads-up: kernel messages show repeated `mlx5_core: SRQ QP 0x2f: completion timeout` and NIC resets.
Leon: here's the tail of the driver log from n17-02:
```
[  12.345678] mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: mlx5_core: ERR: link recovery triggered
[  12.346890] rdma: mlx5_rxe: qp 0x2f retry exceeding
[  12.347001] oom-killer: kill proc 1234 (runtime) score 987
```
Maya: thanks. Customer-impact-bot, any customer-facing metrics?
Cust-Impact-Bot: Affected cohorts: 3 active tenants (payments-api, search-svc, chat-infra). 502 spikes correlate with node flaps; estimated 2k failed requests in last 15m. No SLA breach yet but error budget burn accelerating.
Karen: Confirmed: k8s shows containers restarting due to OOM and liveness probes failing. Node n17-03 shows `GpuProcess: CUDA: out of memory` in container logs.
Aj: I can repro memory growth in a model replica under the current KV cache policy. Looks like heavy retransmit causes KV cache misses and replicas rebuildserting large contexts -> mem spike.
Leon: immediate mitigation idea: 1) take n17-03 out of serving pool, 2) enable fallback model variant with lower memory footprint, 3) throttle request burst to that rack. Can we do canary fallback?
Maya: Agree. Aj - cordon/drain n17-03 and scale up spare capacity in other racks. I'll flip routing policy to avoid rack-17 for golden-tenants.
Aj: `kubectl drain n17-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` running. Eviction in progress.
infra-bot: Autoscaler triggered extra nodes in us-west-2, added 4 nodes to dedicated pool.
Leon: Also flip kvcache eviction to aggressive in the runtime config to avoid large context rebuilds: `PATCH /runtime/config {"kvcache":{"max_entry_size":64MB,"eviction_policy":"lru_aggressive"}}`
Maya: Doing that now. Rolling patch to serving runtime in rack-17. Response stream shows immediate reduction in mem pressure on n17-02.
Aj: RDMA diagnostics across the rack show asymmetric loss: path to TOR-5 shows 2-3% pkt loss and repeated probe timeouts. Might be a flapping link on leaf switch. Ticket to networking already created (NET-5921).
Karen: Customer impact: search-svc and chat-infra saw degraded p95 latency and a small fraction of 502s. payments-api was affected for ~7 minutes during the peak. Notified sales CS — they want ETA.
Leon: For short-term customer messaging: "We detected transient network fabric instability impacting request routing in a subset of serving nodes; we’ve isolated affected nodes and failed over traffic. Engineers are investigating root cause and prioritizing recovery. No sustained data loss." Keep it terse.
Maya: Handoff: I'm taking the incident for the next 4 hours. Current state: n17-03 drained, kvcache patched, model fallback enabled for heavy-context workloads, routing avoids rack-17 for sensitive tenants, autoscaler added capacity. Next steps: follow NET-5921, watch for link flaps and CRC counters, validate no regression in p99 for golden-tenants.
Leon: Adding checklist for postmortem:
- Timeline of node flaps and retransmit metrics
- Why KV cache eviction threshold not triggered earlier
- Assess if quantization/profiles could limit memory blowup during retransmit storms
- Network switch firmware/port flaps and whether link-level backoff worked as expected
- Customer impact timeline and messages

Maya: I'll assemble timeline and grab `perf` dumps from the runtime. Aj, keep NET updated and paste switch port counters here when available.
Aj: switch counters from TOR-5 port 48:
```
ifInErrors: 0
ifOutErrors: 0
ifInUcastPkts: 1234567
ifOutUcastPkts: 1234500
ifInDiscards: 3456
ifOutDiscards: 0
crcErrors: 7
```
Aj: CRC errors + probe suppression correlate with those timestamps. suspect intermittent SFP/optics issue under load.
Maya: Good triage. I'll mark incident status as "mitigated" with reduced customer impact, but keep pager open until NET clears or we swap optics.
SRE-PagerBot: Incident INC-2026-1789 status updated: Mitigated -> Monitoring. Next oncall: @Karen in 3h.
Karen: Acknowledge. I'll take next watch and follow NET ticket. Please drop any late artifacts (logs, timeline) into the incident doc.
Leon: one more note for post-ops: consider adding automatic serving fallback on repeated RDMA retransmit threshold to avoid cascade OOMs. Filing RFC.
Maya: thanks everyone. closing comms thread here; live ops continue in thread INC-2026-1789-ops. :thumbsup:
